subject: Career
title: Lying on Resumes: The Real Risk
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Lying on Resumes: The Real Risk.

hook.text: A survey found 78% of candidates have lied or considered lying on their resume.

buildup.text: Common fabrications: inflated titles, extended dates, fake degrees, phantom skills.

discovery.text: Background check companies verify employment dates, degrees, and sometimes references.

twist.text: Yahoo's CEO was fired after his fake CS degree was exposed. Seniority doesn't protect you.

climax.text: The risk isn't just getting caught once. It's living with a ticking clock forever.

punchline.text: A real story always beats a fake credential.

quiz.question: What happened to Yahoo's CEO regarding resume fraud?
options: Fired after a fake degree was exposed

details.summary: Resume fabrication ranges from minor embellishments to complete credential invention, and all forms carry significant risk. Background checks, reference calls, and increasingly sophisticated verification technology catch most lies.
details.whyItMatters: The short-term temptation to embellish is vastly outweighed by the long-term career destruction when fabrications are discovered, and discovery is becoming more frequent.
takeaways: Background verification technology catches most credential fabrications
Termination for resume fraud can happen years after hiring
Honest framing of genuine experience is more sustainable than fabrication

faq.question: What are the most common types of resume fabrication that employers catch?
faq.answer: Inflated job titles, false degree claims, extended employment dates to cover gaps, and invented certifications are the most frequently caught. Education verification is nearly universal for professional roles, and employment date verification is standard at most companies.

faq.question: What happens when resume fabrication is discovered after being hired?
faq.answer: Most companies terminate immediately regardless of job performance, as it is considered a breach of trust. The discovery often damages your professional reputation within the industry. In some fields like healthcare and finance, it can result in legal consequences and loss of professional licenses.
